description:
Project: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (Serving Runtime Performance: Kernel + Scheduling).

Goal: Reduce p95 tail latency for latency-sensitive traffic when co-scheduled with long prompts by implementing and validating a short/long prompt-aware scheduling policy in Redwood’s inference runtime. The prototype will introduce a queueing and dispatch policy that distinguishes prefill-heavy (long context) requests from short/interactive requests, prioritizes latency-sensitive work without starving throughput-heavy work, and remains stable under bursty traffic.

Scope:
- Runtime scheduler changes (queue classification, dispatch policy, fairness/starvation bounds, backpressure behavior).
- Instrumentation and observability (per-class queue depth, wait time, service time, prefill/decode split, tail breakdown).
- Benchmarking and regression gating (mixed prompt-length distributions, customer-like traces, canary comparisons).
- Rollout plan (feature flag, staged canary in perf-canary + limited production, rollback criteria).

Out of scope (initial prototype):
- Major kernel rewrites; any kernel work is limited to enabling stable measurements (e.g., avoiding measurement artifacts) and ensuring scheduler changes don’t trigger pathological kernel selection.
- Customer-facing API changes.

Stakeholders:
- Primary Eng: Sofia Ivanova (EM Scheduling), Lena Fischer, Marcus Reed, Omar El-Sayed, Julian Moore.
- Kernel consult/review: Hiro Tanaka, Grace Kim, Yuki Sato.
- Perf & evals: Jonas Weber (perf program), Rina Kobayashi (bench harness).
- SRE/ops: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Aisha Bello, Tomáš Novák, Peter Holtz.
- Program/coordination: Talia Benson.
- Product alignment (latency/SLO implications): Lauren Bishop (Dedicated), Paula Mendes (Rollouts).

Timeline (typical 8–10 weeks):
1) Problem framing + design review (week 1–2): define “mixed workload” targets, success metrics, fairness constraints.
2) Prototype implementation behind flag (week 3–5): classification + dispatch policy + instrumentation.
3) Benchmark + tuning (week 5–7): synthetic + trace-based suites; iterate thresholds/weights.
4) Canary + guarded rollout (week 7–9): perf-canary, limited prod slice; dashboards + rollback.
5) Decision + harden (week 9–10): ADR for adopting policy, follow-on tasks, retro.

Key deliverables:
- Confluence design spec + ADR(s) documenting policy and trade-offs.
- Linear project + execution tickets.
- GitHub PR set implementing scheduler changes, metrics, tests, and benchmark harness updates.
- Dashboards/runbooks updates and operational guidance.
- Evidence artifacts: benchmark reports, canary readouts, incident/support follow-ups (if any).

files.description: Primary design doc: problem statement, workload taxonomy (short vs long), proposed scheduling algorithm(s), starvation/fairness guarantees, configuration knobs, and success metrics (p95/p99, throughput impact).
Heuristics doc: how requests are classified (prompt length thresholds, predicted prefill cost, customer tier hints), failure modes, and safe defaults.

ADR capturing the decision to proceed with a short/long prompt-aware scheduler (alternatives considered: FIFO, SRPT approximation, queue partitioning, token-based fairness), and the rationale for the chosen prototype.
Performance standard update proposing required mixed-workload benchmark scenarios and pass/fail gates (including acceptable throughput regression bounds).
Benchmark plan: distributions, trace replays, model set, hardware SKUs, metrics to record, and how results will be compared against baseline and competing policies.
Profiling playbook additions: how to capture scheduler timelines, interpret queueing metrics, and avoid common measurement pitfalls (warmup, batching effects, kernel selection confounders).
Spec for dashboards: per-class queue depth, wait time, p95 breakdown, saturation signals, and alerts for starvation/backlog growth during canary.
SRE guidance: how to interpret tail latency changes with the new scheduler, what to watch during rollouts, and recommended rollback triggers.
Known issues page tracking early prototype risks (e.g., misclassification, long-prompt starvation, burst oscillations) and mitigations/workarounds.
Draft release note entry describing the feature-flagged scheduler prototype, default behavior, and any operator-visible changes.
Working doc with weekly notes, open questions, policy experiments, and links to Linear issues, PRs, and benchmark runs.
Sheet-style artifact: tables of baseline vs prototype p50/p95/p99, throughput, GPU utilization, and queueing metrics across scenarios/hardware.
Canary readout doc: rollout slice, time window, dashboards, regressions found, go/no-go recommendation, and rollback criteria.
Brainstorm doc comparing FIFO, two-queue priority, weighted fair queueing, and SRPT-like heuristics; includes pros/cons and parameter ideas.
SRE checklist for rollout: dashboards to pin, alerts to enable, on-call staffing notes, and quick rollback steps.
Slides for design review: motivation, example timelines, preliminary benchmark graphs, decision points, and next steps.
Umbrella Linear project issue: Mixed-workload scheduler prototype—goals, non-goals, milestones, and links to spec/bench artifacts.
Implement request classification (short vs long) with conservative defaults; includes acceptance criteria and unit tests.
Prototype two-queue scheduling policy with starvation bounds and configurable weights; gated by feature flag.
Add per-class queueing metrics (wait time histograms, queue depth gauges) and tracing hooks for mixed-workload scheduler decisions.
Mixed workload perf suite: add new benchmark scenario definitions and CI gate thresholds for the runtime perf pipeline.
Integrate scheduler feature flag into config system with safe rollout toggles; document default-off behavior.
Implement backpressure changes to avoid priority inversion under overload (e.g., class-based admission control).
Create dashboard panels for mixed-workload tail breakdown and queueing metrics; align with SRE alerting.
Canary plan + rollback criteria issue; includes definition of success metrics, monitoring, and approval checklist.
Run trace-based replay benchmarks using representative customer distributions; attach results and analysis.
Fairness validation: ensure long prompts do not starve; add simulation tests and guardrail metrics for the mixed-workload scheduler.
Post-prototype decision issue: write ADR + decide whether to graduate to default-on for specific tiers/routes.
PR: Add scheduler feature flag plumbing and config surface (default off), including docs/comments and basic integration tests.
PR: Introduce request classification module (prompt-length thresholds + predicted prefill cost stub) with unit tests.
PR: Implement two-queue dispatch policy (short-first with fairness window) in runtime scheduler; includes microbench tests.
PR: Add starvation guardrails (max wait bound, periodic long-queue service) and metrics to detect starvation.
PR: Scheduler instrumentation—trace spans for enqueue/dequeue, per-class queue depth, and wait time histograms.
PR: Perf suite updates for mixed prompt-length distributions; adds scenario definitions and baseline comparison harness.
PR: Add new benchmark runner for mixed workload replay and generate standardized output tables/plots for p95 analysis.
PR: Extend canary job to run A/B comparisons (baseline vs scheduler flag on) and publish summary to dashboards.
PR: Backpressure tweaks—separate admission control thresholds by class to prevent long prompts from inflating short queue latency.
PR: Fix priority inversion bug discovered during load test (short requests blocked behind a long prefill batch); adds regression test.
PR: Documentation updates in-code and config examples for operators enabling the scheduler prototype.
PR: Add dashboard JSON templates/panels for mixed-workload queueing metrics and tail breakdown.
PR: Improve classifier using rolling EWMA of observed prefill time to refine short/long split; includes safeguards and fallback.
PR: Add simulation test harness for fairness/starvation across synthetic arrival patterns; CI gating for regressions.
PR: Optimize scheduler lock contention after adding per-class queues; includes profiling results and before/after metrics.
PR: Add structured logging for scheduler decisions (sampled) to support on-call debugging.
